answer: A proof-of-work leader election mechanism builds Sybil resistance by requiring each identity to solve computationally expensive puzzles that create a computational bridge between identities and verifiable work. New identities must climb a cryptographic ledge by demonstrating genuine resource expenditure before gaining voting rights. This creates a cost structure where attackers face an economic ridge of escalating computational costs proportional to the number of fake identities they attempt to spawn, making large-scale identity forgery prohibitively expensive.
